content:
Aiyana Brooks-Tan
Junior Frontend / Full-Stack Developer
Dublin, Ireland | aiyana.brookstan@example.com | +353 55 555 0404
github.com/aiyana-bt-example | aiyana-bt.example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Early-career developer with experience building accessible React interfaces and a strong project foundation in TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL. Applied accessibility improvements to a production React news site and developed Tidewatch, a full-stack web app tested with screen readers. Familiar with Jest, React Testing Library and Storybook.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS
Backend and databases: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL
Testing and tools: Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook, Git/GitHub, Figma
Other: Web accessibility (WCAG 2.1)

EXPERIENCE
Frontend Developer (part-time, freelance) | Self-employed | Oct 2025–Present
- Built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js, React and Tailwind CSS; deployed on Vercel.
- Made updates to two WordPress sites.

Teaching Assistant, Web Development Lab | Liffey Institute of Technology | Spring 2025
- Supported approximately 30 first-year students during one semester of web development labs.

Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media, Dublin | May 2024–Aug 2024
- Worked with the web team on the company’s React news site.
- Fixed accessibility issues across 20+ components, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels.
- Built a reusable, keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery and documented it with Storybook stories.
- Wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library.

Barista (part-time during studies) | Corner Bean Cafe, Dublin | 2021–2025

SELECTED PROJECTS
Tidewatch | Final Year Project | 2024–2025
- Developed an accessible web app showing tides, water temperature and weather for sea swimmers around the Irish coast.
- Built the frontend with React and TypeScript, and an API with Node.js and Express to cache data from public weather and tide APIs; used PostgreSQL for user favourites.
- Tested with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
- Earned 82% (First Class) and presented the project at the college showcase.
- Technologies: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Chart.js, Jest.

Yoga Studio Booking Site | Freelance | 2025
- Built marketing pages and a class timetable with booking requests sent by email. Used static generation and Markdown files for content; deployed on Vercel.
- Technologies: Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, Vercel.

Study Buddy | Group Project | 2023
- Built the React frontend and login screens for a study-session matching app as part of a four-person team; other team members developed the API and database.
- Technologies: React, JavaScript, Firebase Authentication.

Transit Delay Notifier | Student Hackathon | 2024
- Built the frontend for a transit delay notifier with a three-person team in a 24-hour hackathon; the team placed second.

EDUCATION
BSc (Hons) Computing – Software Development | Liffey Institute of Technology | 2021–2025
First Class Honours
Relevant modules: Web Development, Databases, Human-Computer Interaction, Software Testing, Data Structures & Algorithms

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Mandarin (conversational)

VOLUNTEERING
Run social media for a sea swimming club.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a well-structured, readable early-career CV with a clear React/TypeScript and accessibility focus. The strongest evidence is specific and credible: accessibility fixes across 20+ components, screen-reader testing with NVDA and VoiceOver, a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100, Storybook documentation, and a First Class degree. The addition of the teaching-assistant role and selected projects improves completeness. The main content limitation is that some claims are broader than the evidence supports, while several relevant areas—semantic HTML, responsive layouts, Git workflows, authentication/security awareness, and project impact—are not explained in enough detail. The CV also presents the candidate as a full-stack developer, although backend experience is currently project-based rather than professional.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is highly ATS-readable: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, plain text dates, and recognizable keywords such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub, Storybook, WCAG, and Next.js. The skills are grouped logically and the portfolio links are easy to identify. AI screening probability is good, approximately 82–88%, for junior React/TypeScript roles. Screening may be weaker for this specific vacancy because the CV does not explicitly mention semantic HTML, responsive layouts, Git-based workflows, authentication/security fundamentals, or end-to-end testing. Do not add unsupported terms such as NestJS, Playwright, AWS, Docker, OWASP, GDPR, or WCAG 2.2.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's frontend, TypeScript, accessibility, testing, Storybook, Next.js, wellness, and project-based Node.js/PostgreSQL requirements. The Tidewatch project is particularly relevant to Verdane Care's patient-facing and accessibility focus, and the yoga-studio booking project provides relevant wellness and booking experience. The teaching-assistant experience also supports the mentoring aspect of the role. However, the candidate's material does not demonstrate 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, end-to-end testing, OWASP/security awareness, AWS or Docker, analytics/A-B testing, or German/Croatian. The CV should not imply that these requirements are met. Backend experience should remain clearly identified as project-based.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Professional Summary, change “Applied accessibility improvements to a production React news site” to “Applied accessibility improvements to a React news site” unless the candidate can substantiate that it was a production site. The original candidate information confirms a company React news site but does not explicitly confirm the “production” claim.

MINOR — In the Professional Summary, make the project-based nature of backend experience explicit without weakening the match. For example, change “with a strong project foundation in TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL” to “with project-based experience using TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL.”

MINOR — In the Technical Skills section, change “Web accessibility (WCAG 2.1)” to “Web accessibility: keyboard navigation, colour contrast, ARIA labels, screen-reader testing (NVDA, VoiceOver), WCAG 2.1.” Every item is supported by the candidate information and this better matches the accessibility emphasis of the advertisement.

MINOR — In the Experience section under “Frontend Developer (part-time, freelance),” change “Built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js, React and Tailwind CSS; deployed on Vercel” to “Built and deployed a yoga-studio booking website using Next.js, React and Tailwind CSS; implemented marketing pages, a class timetable, static generation and email booking requests.” This uses the fuller supported project evidence and improves alignment with patient-booking functionality.

MINOR — In the Experience section under “Teaching Assistant, Web Development Lab,” change the bullet to “Supported approximately 30 first-year students during one semester of web-development labs, answering questions and helping them resolve practical problems.” This remains truthful while making the mentoring relevance more visible.

MINOR — In the Tidewatch project, retain the existing accessibility and backend evidence but add the supported implementation detail to the first two bullets: “Developed an accessible React and TypeScript web app showing tides, water temperature and weather for sea swimmers around the Irish coast” and “Built a Node.js/Express API to cache data from public weather and tide APIs and used PostgreSQL for user favourites.” This improves keyword matching for React/TypeScript, Node.js APIs, and SQL databases without implying professional backend experience.

MINOR — In the Technical Skills section, retain “Git/GitHub,” but do not label the candidate as having a Git-based workflow unless the candidate can substantiate that experience. The current CV names the tools but does not describe branching, pull requests, code review, or other workflow practices.
critique.critical_issues: Potential unsupported claim: the Professional Summary describes Harbourline Media's React news site as “production.” The original candidate information confirms a company React news site but does not explicitly confirm that it was a production site. Remove or qualify “production” to avoid overstating experience.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, well-structured early-career CV with strong evidence of React, TypeScript, accessibility, testing, Node.js and PostgreSQL experience. The Professional Summary is targeted and the Experience and Selected Projects sections provide credible context for project-based work. The accessibility achievements are particularly relevant and specific, including work across 20+ components, screen-reader testing and a Lighthouse score of 100. The main content limitation is that the CV presents a strong junior profile, while the role asks for 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience. This is a candidate-experience gap rather than a document defect. The CV also does not provide evidence of end-to-end testing, web security fundamentals or health-data privacy awareness.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, readable bullets and highly relevant keywords such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook, WCAG 2.1 and Next.js. It should parse well in most ATS platforms, with a high but not certain AI-screening probability because the candidate does not meet or demonstrate several must-have requirements. ATS alignment would be slightly stronger if the GitHub and portfolio entries were written as complete URLs and if the CV explicitly connected Git/GitHub to development workflows where supported. Do not add unsupported keywords such as Playwright, NestJS, AWS, Docker, OWASP or GDPR.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's patient-facing accessibility focus and with the company's emphasis on simple, inclusive user experiences. Relevant evidence includes accessible React work, keyboard navigation, colour contrast, ARIA labels, NVDA and VoiceOver testing, Storybook documentation, a wellness-related booking site, and a full-stack project using Node.js/Express and PostgreSQL. The CV shows the following requirement statuses: 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript web-application experience is a gap; the candidate has an internship and freelance experience but not 2+ years of professional experience. Backend Node.js and SQL experience is shown through Tidewatch. Semantic HTML, responsive layouts and accessibility basics are reasonably supported through HTML5/CSS3 and the accessibility work, although semantic HTML and responsive layouts are not stated explicitly. Automated testing and Git-based workflows are only partially supported: unit testing and Git/GitHub are shown, but end-to-end testing is not. Web-security fundamentals and OWASP awareness are not evidenced. Willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements is not evidenced in the candidate material. Fluent English is shown. German or Croatian is not shown. Next.js is shown. Wellness-related experience is shown through the yoga-studio booking site, although there is no healthcare or regulated-environment experience. AWS/Docker and analytics/A/B testing are not shown. Storybook experience is shown.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS/clarity improvements:
1. In the contact-information line at the top of the CV, replace “github.com/aiyana-bt-example | aiyana-bt.example.com” with complete, consistently formatted URLs such as “https://github.com/aiyana-bt-example | https://aiyana-bt.example.com”. This improves link recognition by ATS and recruiters.
2. In the Technical Skills section, change “Git/GitHub” to “Git, GitHub” so both keywords are independently parsed. Do not describe this as a Git workflow unless the candidate can substantiate workflow experience.
3. In the Tidewatch project bullet beginning “Built a Node.js/Express API,” retain the explicit wording “Node.js/Express API” and “PostgreSQL” as currently written; these are strong matches for the job and should not be shortened or hidden in the technology list.
4. In the Experience section under “Frontend Developer (part-time, freelance),” change “Made updates to two WordPress sites.” to “Maintained and updated two WordPress sites.” only if “maintained” accurately reflects the work performed. Otherwise retain the current wording. This would make the contribution slightly more professional without adding unsupported scope.
